topics.title: Coursework & Assessment Categories
topics.summary: Under Senate Policy DocID 79331 §2.1.1, assessments are categorized into four levels (Category A: AI Prohibited, Category B: AI Minimal, Category C: AI Permitted, Category D: AI-Integrated) by Course Unit Directors and clearly stated in unit specifications and Canvas briefs (§2.1.3). Students may choose not to use AI for Categories A, B, and C without disadvantage, but this choice does not apply to Category D assessments which assess AI learning outcomes (§2.1.2). In Category A, all AI use including proofreading and text editing is prohibited; in Category B, AI is restricted to presentation only (fluency, grammar, spelling, formatting) without altering student ideas, arguments, or conclusions.
topics.scope: Undergraduate and postgraduate taught coursework assessments
actions: Check the designated AI category on your assessment brief on Canvas before beginning coursework.
If undertaking a Category B or C assessment, note that you may choose not to use AI tools personal to you.
Remember that Category D assessments require AI use to meet the unit's intended learning outcomes.

topics.title: Acknowledgment & Citation
topics.summary: Under University Library referencing guidance, students must cite generative AI tools when using text or images directly in their work following 'Cite them Right' conventions. Where asked or deemed appropriate, students should include an overview acknowledgement at the start of work or in a footnote. An appendix detailing relevant prompts, outputs, generation dates, and modification statements is required when referencing AI as personal communication or when instructed by School guidance. Using tools for basic grammar and spell checking does not require acknowledgement unless School guidance requires it.
topics.scope: Assessed coursework submissions, dissertations, and project reports
actions: If you use AI-generated text or images directly in your work, provide an in-text citation and reference list entry following 'Cite them Right'.
Where asked or felt appropriate, include an overview acknowledgement at the start of your work or in a footnote describing tools used.
When referencing AI as personal communication or instructed by your School, attach an appendix with relevant prompts, outputs, dates, and modifications.

topics.title: Data Protection & Copyright Restrictions
topics.summary: Under Senate Policy DocID 79331 §2.2.1(c), students must not upload University-owned copyright materials (such as lecture recordings, slides, handouts, or examination questions) to external commercial AI tools. Under §2.2.2, students are explicitly permitted to upload session recordings into University-provided Microsoft 365 Copilot for study support. Under §2.3.1, staff members who use AI in Teaching and Learning activities must adhere to the University's AI Guidelines, and only the University-provided Microsoft 365 Copilot service may be used for student-identifiable or confidential data.

Use University-provided Microsoft 365 Copilot if uploading taught session recordings for study assistance (§2.2.2).
Teaching staff handling student-identifiable or confidential data must exclusively use University-provided Microsoft 365 Copilot (§2.3.1).

topics.title: Research, Data Synthesis & Publication
topics.summary: Under StaffNet Research Guidelines, any use of AI to synthesise research data must be completely transparent, and fabricating or falsifying data with AI constitutes research misconduct. Corresponding authors carry ultimate responsibility for publication credibility and must declare significant AI assistance. Researchers reviewing papers or grants must preserve peer review confidentiality and never upload unpublished manuscripts into external AI services.
topics.scope: Postgraduate research, academic publications, data synthesis, and peer review
actions: Verify all literature and citations against original sources and transparently declare any synthesised research data.
Never upload unpublished manuscripts or funding proposals under peer review into external AI services.

claims.text: University AI Guidelines | AI Hub | StaffNet | The University of Manchester

evidence.quote:
The University recognises the potential of AI to power research and innovation and encourages applications that adhere to the principles for appropriate use. It will seek to support appropriate use by providing equitable access to AI technology and training.
Synthesising data
Any use of AI to generate data should be completely transparent. Legitimate uses may include synthesising datasets for use in research on scarce or sensitive data, imputing missing data in real datasets or conducting research on generative AI. In such cases the distinction between real and synthesised data should be made clear, and the methods used should be detailed. Using AI to fabricate or manipulate data such as experimental measurements, interview texts or research images, without clear declaration, constitutes research misconduct.

additionalTopics.title: Malpractice Detection, Viva Voce & Case Handling
additionalTopics.summary: The University does not currently use software claiming to detect generative AI; Turnitin alone does not confirm malpractice and academic judgment is required. Under Academic Malpractice Procedure DocID 639 §4.4.2, where indicators raise concerns of commissioned work without direct evidence, or available information does not satisfy the balance of probabilities, a viva voce can be arranged in agreement with the School Officer to demonstrate authorship; it does not contribute to the mark. If held, it should not normally take place more than 30 working days after the assessment feedback deadline (§4.4.3.1); the student should receive at least five working days notice explaining its nature, purpose and potential outcomes (§4.4.3.2). Accompaniment by a person of the student’s choice is for support only without participation (§4.4.3.4), and reasonable adjustments must be made (§4.4.3.5). The viva itself cannot impose a penalty (§4.4.4.2); case handling follows the applicable AUO/SDP/UDP procedures (§5.1–5.5).

evidence.quote:
4.4.2. If there is a concern, based on indicators of malpractice, that a student may have
        commissioned a piece of work from a third party, but there is no direct evidence of this,
        or the information available does not satisfy the balance of probabilities, then in
        agreement with the School Officer a viva voce can be arranged to give the student the
        opportunity to demonstrate that they:

       4.4.2.1.   Produced the work;

       4.4.2.2.   Undertook the reading and research themselves;

       4.4.2.3.   Undertook the preparatory work themselves;

       4.4.2.4.   Understand what they have written.

   4.4.3. If a viva voce is held, the following principles shall be met:

       4.4.3.1.   If a viva voce is to be conducted it should not normally take place more than
              30 working days after the assessment feedback deadline.

       4.4.3.2.    The student should be given at least five working days’ notice of the
              requirement to attend the viva voce. An explanation of what a viva voce is, the
              purpose of it and the potential outcomes should be outlined in the invitation. It
              should be made clear that the viva voce is arranged due to the detection of
              potential academic malpractice and it is to allow the student an opportunity to
              demonstrate that the work is their own; it will not contribute to any mark obtained
              for the piece of work.

       4.4.3.3.    Two members of academic staff (at least one of whom must be a subject
              specialist) must conduct the viva voce; this will normally be the School Officer and
              the examiner of the assessment.

       4.4.3.4.    The student may be accompanied by a person of their choice for support only
              (normally a fellow student, member of staff or Students’ Union representative).
              Any individual accompanying the student should under no circumstances
              participate in the viva voce.
evidence.title: Academic Malpractice Procedure
evidence.location: Section 4.4 Contract cheating, Paragraphs 4.4.2–4.4.3.4, Page 9; Extracted text SHA256 db1ed4db97896ef1f771a937943e2402de1a954b0b0a56c53a781efa68c9af77; original binding lines 484–518; characters 31340–33372

evidence.quote:
4.4.3.5.   Reasonable adjustments must be made to ensure that candidates with
                additional support needs are not disadvantaged for reasons relating to a long-term
                medical condition, sensory impairment, specific learning difficulty and /or disability.

         4.4.3.6.    The viva voce will not normally exceed 45 minutes.

         4.4.3.7.   Depending on situational circumstances, the viva voce can be conducted via
                video link.

         4.4.3.8.   Intensive questions are expected. The questions asked should provide the
                student with the opportunity to demonstrate that the work is their own.

         4.4.3.9.    An accurate record of the viva voce should be taken; this record may be used
                to form the evidence base for any future disciplinary hearing. It may be necessary
                for an administrative member of staff to be present at the viva voce to make the
                record. The student is entitled to have a copy of the record.

     4.4.4. The viva voce can have one of two outcomes:

         4.4.4.1.   The staff conducting the viva voce will confirm that they accept that the student
                wrote the work in question; no further action will be taken. The work should then
                be marked on its own merit, if it has not already been marked.

         4.4.4.2.   If the staff conducting the viva voce still remain doubtful of the authorship of
                the work in question, or the student admits that it is not their work, then the case
                should be referred for disciplinary action. The viva voce, in itself, will not result in
                a penalty being applied; a penalty can only be applied by a disciplinary panel.
